DEFECT: ItemFactsProvider has an option `mark_fixed` (default False) that adds a fixed-thing sentence to the narrator's THINGS block. The bench threads it from `variation['item_facts']['mark_fixed']` into `provider_for`, but in RUNTIME mode the bench builds its provider with `build_capture_provider(state)` (bench/core.py in `run_scene`, and again for `loaded_provider` in the save/load reload factory), and `build_capture_provider` in storygame/runtime/capture.py takes no options. So a runtime-mode variation with mark_fixed true never reaches the narrator (recorded prompts contain no marker).

FIX: (1) `build_capture_provider(state, *, mark_fixed=False)` in capture.py passes `mark_fixed=mark_fixed` to `ItemFactsProvider.from_environment`. The default must stay False so storygame/web_demo.py (two callers) and tests/test_runtime_capture.py behave exactly as before; do not edit web_demo.py. (2) In bench/core.py both runtime call sites pass `mark_fixed=bool(variation.get('item_facts', {}).get('mark_fixed', False))`. Use the variation in scope at each site (read the code; the reload factory is inside run_scene so `variation` is available).

TESTS: edit tests/test_bench_runtime_mode.py. It already monkeypatches `core.build_capture_provider` around line 239-253 to inspect the provider. Add a test (hermetic, no network, stubbed like the existing ones) that runs a runtime-mode bench scene with a variation whose item_facts has mark_fixed true and asserts the provider built for the run has `mark_fixed is True`, and a second assertion that a variation without it gives False. Also add to tests/test_runtime_capture.py? NO (not owned); instead assert the default in the same bench test file by calling `build_capture_provider(state)` directly and checking `.mark_fixed is False`, and `build_capture_provider(state, mark_fixed=True).mark_fixed is True` (state built the way tests/test_runtime_capture.py builds one; copy the few setup lines).

HOW TO RUN: confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)"` prints a path inside the cwd. Tests: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov tests/test_bench_runtime_mode.py tests/test_runtime_capture.py tests/test_fixed_thing_marker.py tests/test_web_demo.py. Also `-k "bench or capture or item_facts"` over tests/. Ruff: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix and -m ruff format on every file you changed. Reply with the files changed.
